newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish car sales soar nearly 40 pct in 11 months.
newsitem.headline: Polish car sales soar nearly 40 pct in 11 months.

text.p: New car sales in Poland jumped 39.7 percent in the first 11 months of 1996 compared with the same period last year, showing the biggest growth rate in Europe, an independent monitoring agency reported.

A monthly survey by the private Samar agency, which monitors the domestic car market, showed 347,845 new passenger cars were registered in January-October, compared with 248,947 in the same period last year.
During the 11 months, the number of newly-registered delivery vehicles jumped by nearly 60 percent to 45,045 units, compared with the same period last year.
Samar, quoting figures by the Association des Constructeurs Europeens d'Automobiles, said Poland had the fastest new car sales growth rate in Europe.
It said Poland was followed by Norway and Ireland, where car registration growth reached 34.7 percent and 32.2 percent over the period, with 117,300 and 114,200 cars sold respectively.
Germany, the leader in new car sales volume, registered an estimated 3,263,300 passenger cars in the January-November period, 5.9 percent more than last year.
In Poland, the domestic unit of Fiat Spa led the market with 145,700 cars and a 42 percent market share.
Other top sellers include Daewoo-FSO, a unit of South Korea's Daewoo Corp, General Motors' German unit Adam Opel AG and Renault.
Samar director Wojciech Drzewiecki earlier said that robust car sales were fuelled by growth in real wages and expansion of credit by banks.
